insights.title: Division, quotient/remainder and scope boundaries
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie begins with aligned arithmetic, then cubic/linear division and several equivalent worked routes;its1A set moves from linear to quadratic divisors. YM separates linear and quadratic division and explicitly includes zero columns, nonmonic divisors and other variable letters. YMExample15 only asks a remainder although its solution works a quotient;Example16 asks both. GoldiePrompt3 asks why a reduced remainder has lower degree. These are different required outputs, not interchangeable answer fields.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2023P2Q1(a) and2024P2Q5(a) give observed division structures. The latter source p(x) defect remains registered; its existence does not undermine exact division of the intended polynomial. Official awards, not the quantity of textbook working, decide later method credit. The three-brackets-without-working restriction in2023Q1(b) belongs to the connected factorisation part, not every division task.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: GradeA11 explicitly permits degree-at-most-four dividends and linear/quadratic divisors. It does not impose that dividend limit on unrelated multiplication or theorem evaluation. Nonmonic scaling, sparse columns and linear versus scalar remainder are meaningful difficulty branches;larger coefficients alone are not. No numeric grade parameter domain is set here.
insights.pitfalls: YMExample14 changes its dividend constant in a later displayed identity;Try15 omits requested quotients in the key. These source defects are recorded. Independent reconstruction P=DQ+R and degree checks can catch both arithmetic and wrong-output mistakes. The textbook cautions do not establish an examiner-reported rate of those errors.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Both books provide substantial forward division practice;Goldie has explicit conceptual remainder-degree support. A remainder-only theorem exercise does not cover asked quotient recovery, and a surrounding quadratic-division heading does not makeYMTry16Q2(c) a quadratic-divisor question. Supporting high-power arithmetic must not create out-of-scope division coverage.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose distinct output contracts for quotient only,remainder only and both, with an invariant reconstruction check. Preserve linear/nonmonic and quadratic remainder branches. Treat supplied quotient identities separately from freely chosen algorithms; derive future diagram/long-division layouts from the original coefficients.

insights.title: Theorem evaluation, inverse constraints and factorisation
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie moves from value tables and integer-candidate tests to factor/solve/sketch chains, then inverse coefficient constraints. YM explicitly contrasts quotient/remainder computation with evaluation without division, then factor proofs, complete factorisation and polynomial solves. Both use nonmonic divisor roots exactly. YM19Q1 adds an unknown exponent;20Q2 uses an unspecifiedR and2R;Goldie1B14/YM23Q3 yield multiple parameter tuples. These are authored structural branches of one constraint-building decision, not a recipe per set of numbers.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2021P2Q1(a)(b),2025P2Q1 and2023P2Q1(b)(c) anchor inverse constraints and factor-to-root chains. Convention037 explicitly denies2023Q1(b)marks for three correct brackets without working; do not infer that all factorisations everywhere have that exact award. Textbooks additionally ask full sketches, exponent recovery or transformed-variable roots that the cited parts do not.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: GradeE10 names single-unknown linear theorem work;C10 broadens coefficient evaluation and polynomial solving;A11 names combined factor/remainder constraints. Nonlinear parameter tuples, parameter-dependent divisor roots and original-variable recovery increase reasoning demands. The title of a harder exercise is not evidence of a higher assessed Bloom level or a grade assigned here.
insights.pitfalls: GoldieExample9 demonstrates that no integer root is not no real root. YMExercise8 needs both distinct roots to prove a quadratic factor. Try27 has a wrong |x| recovery;Exercise18 needs secant/cosine range rejection. ERR10 supports original-variable recovery broadly. Wrong printed factors or copied signs are source defects, not demonstrated learner misconceptions.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Both books provide inverse constraints and factor/solve chains;Goldie adds a richer factor-to-sketch progression, whileYM supplies exponent,composition and trigonometric recovery. Root multiplicity, irreducible real factors and complete original-domain checking need to remain visible. No absence from these textbook families changes the138-demand syllabus map.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose retaining a constraint ledger that distinguishes zero,known,equal and scaled remainders. Verify every recovered tuple in every original condition. Keep inverse recovery and sketch extensions connected where asked. A candidate-root search must record its admitted set and scope of any failure conclusion.
